quizzes.stem: A team's product still calls a model that the documentation lists as deprecated, with a retirement date seven weeks away. Which action fits best?

options.a: Audit usage by API key, then try the recommended replacement on your own cases long before the deadline
options.b: Wait for the day that the model retires, since requests continue to be answered until then without a problem
options.c: Move the workload to a cloud partner, whose retirement schedule will be the same as the vendor's own
options.d: Swap the model id in the configuration and ship at once, because the replacement is the documented one

explanation.a: The audit finds every use, and the replacement is tested on the team's own tasks before the date.
explanation.b: Ruled out because "Requests to retired models will fail" and "Deprecated models are likely to be less reliable than active models".
explanation.c: Ruled out because "Partner-operated platforms (Amazon Bedrock and Google Cloud) set their own retirement schedules".
explanation.d: Ruled out because the new model "refuses settings the old one accepted, changes defaults without an error, and costs more per answer".

quizzes.stem: After a team swaps the model id in its code, every request that sets a non-default temperature comes back with a 400 error. What explains it?

options.a: The old id is still held in a cache, and the cache must be flushed before the request works
options.b: The new model needs a longer timeout than the old one did for the very same request
options.c: The replacement refuses sampling parameters, so they have to stop being sent altogether
options.d: The temperature must now be below a lower ceiling, so the value alone needs to change

explanation.c: A 400 on a sampling setting means the model no longer accepts it, and the fix is to remove it.
explanation.a: Ruled out because "It is not a timeout, a cache that holds the old model, or a value out of range".
explanation.b: Ruled out because "A 400 on one of these is a refusal of the shape of the request", and a longer timeout does not change a refusal.
explanation.d: Ruled out because "The fix is to stop sending it, not to change its value".

quizzes.stem: The regression suite shows the new model with a higher overall pass rate, but one case that must pass now fails. What should the gate do?

options.a: Accept the change, because the overall pass rate is higher and the average is what counts
options.b: Refuse the change, because a single broken requirement blocks it whatever the mean says
options.c: Refuse the change only when the failed case sits in a protected segment, and accept it otherwise
options.d: Accept it and keep a close watch on that case once the change is running in production

explanation.b: A must-pass case is a rule, so one failure refuses the change.
explanation.a: Ruled out because "An average can rise while a case that must pass breaks".
explanation.c: Ruled out because of the rule "If any fails, the change is refused", whatever the segment.
explanation.d: Ruled out because "watching a known failure in production makes customers the test".

quizzes.stem: A staged roll-out is at 25 percent of requests when the error rate passes its limit. What happens next?

options.a: Drop to 5 percent and keep the roll-out running, to gather more evidence from a smaller share
options.b: Hold at 25 percent and investigate, leaving those customers on the new model while the errors continue to arrive
options.c: Advance to 100 percent so that the failure shows up clearly in the data of the whole base
options.d: Send all traffic back to the previous model, which stays available until its own retirement

explanation.d: The limit is passed, so the share goes back to zero and the previous model, still configured, takes the traffic.
explanation.b: Ruled out because "Holding at the stage while errors continue leaves the share of customers who see them where it is".
explanation.c: Ruled out because "Advancing to 100 percent to see the failure in the full data makes every customer the sample".
explanation.a: Ruled out because "Reducing to a smaller share keeps part of the damage on the path".

quizzes.stem: The new model costs about a third more per answer and fixes the refund errors. The product owner asks whether to move. Which message fits the architect's role?

options.a: Recommend staying on the old model, because a higher cost is reason enough to avoid the whole change
options.b: Recommend the move, because the newer model is the one that the vendor has recommended as the replacement
options.c: State the trade: what improves, what the rise takes from the budget, and the date that forces the choice
options.d: Defer the decision until the old model retires, so that the choice is made by the calendar instead

explanation.c: The decision is a trade, and the architect states it with its date.
explanation.b: Ruled out because "A recommended replacement is a starting point, not a decision".
explanation.a: Ruled out because "A rise in cost is a number to put before the owner, not a verdict".
explanation.d: Ruled out because "Waiting for the retirement date hands the decision to the calendar, and gives up the rollback".

quizzes.stem: After a migration, the parser reads the wrong field because the first content block of a reply is thinking text. Which step was missed?

options.a: Lowering max_tokens so that the thinking is cut off before the text of the reply begins
options.b: Choosing the part of the response by its declared type and not by its position in the list
options.c: Turning thinking off by sending the disabled setting, which the new model accepts as before
options.d: Dropping the first block of every reply before parsing, since it always holds only thinking

explanation.b: A reply may begin with thinking blocks, so the parser reads by type.
explanation.a: Ruled out because "`max_tokens` covers thinking plus text, and thinking tokens are billed as output tokens".
explanation.c: Ruled out because the guide lists `thinking: {"type": "disabled"}` among the "five settings that return a 400 error".
explanation.d: Ruled out because "A reply need not begin with thinking text either, so a rule that always drops the first block loses real text".

quizzes.stem: Cost per answer rose after the migration although traffic is unchanged, and the budget was set from the old model's token counts. What does the migration guidance imply?

options.a: Return to the old model, because the budget is fixed and cannot be allowed to change
options.b: Treat the rise as a billing error and ask the provider to correct the charges
options.c: Shorten every prompt until the old budget fits again, whatever happens to quality
options.d: Measure usage again on the replacement, reset the spending plan to it, and report the difference

explanation.d: The price and the token counts both changed, so the baseline is reset.
explanation.b: Ruled out because "A rise in cost per answer after a migration is therefore not a billing error".
explanation.c: Ruled out because "Shortening every prompt until the old budget fits again trades quality for a number that no longer applies".
explanation.a: Ruled out because "a budget that cannot change is a decision to stay on a model whose date is fixed".
